facts.fact: The World Bank's implementation report records 1% of health centres using electronic medical records at 31 October 2025, against 0% at baseline and a 20% target for May 2028; the denominator is the 102 district-level 'centres de santé' only, and a centre counts if at least 30% of its consultations are recorded electronically.

The World Bank's implementation report measures EMR use at district-level health centres ('centres de santé'), recording 1% of the 102 as users at 31 October 2025, and counts 200,000 primary care patients with an electronic medical record available on the same date; it reports no use at any other tier.

The World Bank reports that primary care patients with an electronic medical record available rose from 0 at 25 October 2024 to 200,000 at 31 October 2025 (55% female), against a target of 1,500,000 by May 2028, and that the draft contract for scaling up the EMR had been finalised.

The EMR is financed under Component 4 (USD 46 million) of the IDA-funded Senegal Digital Economy Acceleration Project, of which 4.15% of USD 166.85 million was disbursed by the report's archiving on 21 November 2025; the indicator for a financial viability model integrating digital health costs into national health financing stood at 'No' on 31 October 2025.

The World Bank project approved on 9 February 2023 and closing on 31 May 2028 names adoption of electronic medical records in its development objective and sets costed targets of 20% of health centres using the EMR and 1,500,000 patients with a record by May 2028; it is a project results framework, not a national strategy.
